newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco stocks end lower as blue-chips decline.
newsitem.headline: Morocco stocks end lower as blue-chips decline.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Wednesday 0.19 percent lower as most blue-chip stocks resumed their declines, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 670.68 points, down from 671.93 points on Tuesday.
"Investors are becoming more cautious, they used to make quick gains in short periods, now they are realising things can change," a broker said.

The bourse, which showed an exceptional market capitalisation of 100 billion dirhams ($10.6 billion) in the first quarter of 1997, is expected to stagnate soon, a Moroccan market analyst told Reuters earlier.
ONA, the country's largest private conglomerate, dropped five dirhams to close at 805 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the second largest private conglomerate, fell nine dirhams to 747 dirhams.
In the banking sector, Banque Commerciale Marocaine shed eight dirhams to 862 dirhams.

Credit firms registered falls, including Maroc-Leasing which lost 14 dirhams to 456 dirhams, Credor dropped two dirhams to 813 dirhams, Diac Maroc fell to 714 dirhams, down five dirhams over the previous session.

Among the few gainers were Samir firm, Morocco's main oil refinery, which rose 10 dirhams to 356 dirhams, Banque Marocaine du Commerce et de l'Industrie gained 15 dirhams to 523 dirhams and dairy firm Centrale Laitiere which rose 80 dirhams to 3,180 dirhams.
Total volume traded on the official market stood at 43.9 million dirhams, up from more than 31 million dirhams on Tuesday.
On the over-the-counter market, volume rose to 157.4 million dirhams from 93.8 million on Tuesday.
